---
title: Series
description: "One multichannel run of ordered numeric steps per record, as context or a forecast target."
---

The daily spend of an account is a run of numbers whose order matters: a payment
model can use the last 90 days as context, or forecast the next seven. `Series`
holds one such run per record. Each step carries `channels` numeric values, such
as daily amount spent and daily transaction count. Steps are ordered, not
timestamped; use a [Branch](branch.qmd) with [Period](dateparts.qmd) when the
calendar position of each item matters.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    recent=rf.Series(channels=2, length=90, overflow="tail"),
    next_week=rf.Series(channels=2, horizon=7, mask=True),
)
```

One record:

```yaml
recent:
  - [84.50, 3]
  - [0.00, 0]
  - [12.20, 1]
next_week:
  - [40.00, 2]
  - [0.00, 0]
```

The record shows three days of history and two forecast days; real records carry
the full `length` and `horizon`. Every step in the history is known at the
decision time. Use [Number](number.qmd) for a single value per record and
[Branch](branch.qmd) when each step has fields of different types.

## Input and options

Each valued input must be an Arrow list of numbers when `channels=1`, or a list
of lists or fixed-size lists with exactly `channels` numbers per step. Values
convert to `float64`; integers beyond ±2^53 are rejected. A null, NaN, or
infinite step is unobserved: the rest of the series stays valid, and the encoder
sees which steps were observed. An empty series is `valued`. A non-empty series
with no observed step takes the `other` [value state](index.qmd#value-state).
A null series is `null`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `channels` | required | Positive number of values per step. |
| `length` | `None` | Hard cap on retained steps. `None` keeps the whole series and pads each batch to its longest. |
| `overflow` | `None` | With a finite `length`: `head` (default), `tail`, `random`, or `error`. Rejected when `length` is `None`. |
| `horizon` | `None` | Steps to predict. Required with `mask=True` and rejected otherwise. |
| `n_blocks` | `6` | Number of dilated convolution blocks. |
| `jitter` | `rf.Jitter()` | Training noise on input steps. |
| `objective` | `"l2"` | Forecast loss: mean `"l1"` or `"l2"` error over predicted steps and channels. |

Overflow follows [Branch](branch.qmd): use `tail` for recency-ordered history.
With `random`, training draws a contiguous window of steps and later phases keep
the tail. A forecast target pads to exactly `horizon` steps and rejects a longer
series.

## Encoding

Per-channel statistics learned from training observations standardize the
steps. Standardized steps pass through a linear projection to the model width,
then `n_blocks` residual blocks of two dilated convolutions with dilation
doubling at each block. A masked max-pool collapses the result to one token, so
the field adds one token to its record however long the series is. Padding and
unobserved steps never contribute, and an embedding does not depend on the
padded width of the batch.

With `n_blocks=k`, one token sees `1 + 4 * (2^k - 1)` steps: 253 at the default
of six. Choose `n_blocks` so that this covers the history that matters; steps
beyond it cannot influence the token. Apply `length` to bound memory.

## Learning and output

As a forecast target, `Series` predicts `horizon` steps of `channels` values
from the context of the record. The loss is the `objective` error over target steps
observed in the source, after both sides are standardized per channel.
Predictions are decoded back to source units. MAE and RMSE metrics report in
source units.

Classify a series by pairing it with a sibling target such as
`label=rf.Category(mask=True)`. `embed=True` exports a series embedding of the
model width. See [shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options).

In [prediction output](../reference/prediction-output.qmd), `content` is a list
of `horizon` steps, each a list of `channels` float64 values. The writer emits
exactly `horizon` steps per coordinate. Parquet round-trips these lists,
including inside a `Branch` with null items. As with other decoded fields, read
the shared `state` and `inferred` members to learn whether a series was
reconstructed.
